Right now, as you watch this, your body is quietly rebuilding itself.
hook
In the next twenty-four hours, it will do things that sound impossible.
hook
And the strangest one happens at night, while you sleep. You will never notice it. So let's start with the beat you can feel right now.
heart
Your heart beats about seventy times a minute. That doesn't sound like much.
heart
But there are one thousand, four hundred and forty minutes in a day. So by tomorrow, your heart will beat around one hundred thousand times.
heart
With every beat, tiny valves snap open and shut, so your blood can only flow one way.
heart
In a single day, your heart pumps around seven thousand liters of blood. That's enough to fill about forty bathtubs.
lungs
To keep all that blood full of oxygen, your lungs never take a break.
lungs
You'll breathe around twenty thousand times today, moving more than ten thousand liters of air.
lungs
Deep inside, hundreds of millions of tiny air sacs trade oxygen for carbon dioxide. Spread out flat, they would cover about seventy square meters.
blood
Once your blood picks up that oxygen, it races through your body. One full lap takes about a minute.
blood
That's well over a thousand trips around your body, every single day.
blood
Along the way, red blood cells wear out. So deep inside your bones, new ones are made: about two million every second.
stomach
Meanwhile, your stomach is fighting a battle against itself.
stomach
It's full of acid strong enough to damage your own tissue. The only thing protecting it is a thin layer of mucus.
stomach
So the cells lining your stomach are constantly being replaced. Every few days, you get a brand new lining.
gut
Past your stomach, you're never alone. Your gut is home to around thirty-eight trillion bacteria.
gut
That's roughly as many as all of your own cells. And they help digest food your body can't break down by itself.
kidneys
Further down, two bean-shaped organs are doing the cleaning.
kidneys
Your kidneys filter about one hundred and eighty liters of fluid every day.
kidneys
Then they put almost all of it back, keeping just a liter or two to carry the waste away.
skin
On the outside, your skin is quietly falling apart. You shed tens of thousands of skin cells every single minute.
skin
Don't worry, new ones keep rising from below. Your outer layer of skin replaces itself about once a month.
eyes
Even your eyes are busy. You'll blink around fifteen thousand times today.
eyes
Each blink spreads a fresh layer of tears that cleans your eyes and keeps them from drying out.
cells
Add it all up, and something incredible is happening.
cells
Every day, your body replaces around three hundred and thirty billion cells. That's about one percent of you.
cells
In about three months, you replace roughly thirty trillion cells. Most of them are blood cells.
brain
And your brain? It makes up only about two percent of your body weight, yet it burns around twenty percent of your energy.
night
But remember the strangest thing? It happens at night.
night
When you fall into deep sleep, fluid starts flowing through your brain in slow, rhythmic waves.
night
Scientists think it washes away waste that builds up while you're awake, like a cleaning crew that only works the night shift.
night
Which is one more reason a good night's sleep matters so much.
